social_security.summary: Social Security (and Tier 1 Railroad Retirement) benefits included in federal adjusted gross income are subtracted from Virginia taxable income.

sources.quote: Benefits received under Title II of the Social Security Act and other benefits subject to federal income taxation solely pursuant to § 86 of the Internal Revenue Code.

Virginia law exempts Social Security and Tier 1 Railroad Retirement benefits from taxation. If you were required to include any of your benefits in federal adjusted gross income, subtract that amount on your Virginia return.

public_pension.summary: Virginia taxes state, local and federal civil service pensions like other income; a taxpayer 65 or older may claim the age deduction of up to $12,000, reduced as income rises.
conditions: age deduction of up to $12,000 at 65 or older (born on or before 1 January 1960 for 2025)
reduced $1 for every $1 of adjusted federal adjusted gross income above $50,000 (single) or $75,000 (married)

sources.quote: A deduction in the amount of $ 12,000 for individuals born after January 1, 1939, who have attained the age of 65.

If you or your spouse were born on or before Jan. 1, 1960, you may qualify to claim an age deduction of up to $12,000 each. The age deduction you may claim will depend upon your birth date, filing status, and income.

private_pension.summary: Private pensions, 401(k) and IRA distributions are taxed like other income; the same income-based age deduction of up to $12,000 applies at 65 or older.
conditions: age deduction of up to $12,000 at 65 or older, income-tested

sources.quote: This deduction shall be reduced by $ 1 for every $ 1 that the taxpayer's adjusted federal adjusted gross income exceeds $ 50,000 for single taxpayers or $ 75,000 for married taxpayers.
This deduction shall be reduced by $1 for every $1 that the taxpayer's adjusted federal adjusted gross income exceeds $50,000 for single taxpayers or $75,000 for married taxpayers.

military_retirement.summary: Up to $40,000 of military benefits, including military retirement income, may be subtracted for taxable years beginning on and after 1 January 2025, at any age.
conditions: no other credit, subtraction or deduction for the same income

sources.quote: for taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 2025, up to $40,000 of military benefits.
You can claim a subtraction for certain military benefits. These include: military retirement income received for service in the Armed Forces of the United States

notes: The $40,000 figure is the Code's (§ 58.1-322.02, subdivision 18 c); the Department's subtractions page describes the subtraction without the amount. The age deduction is a general deduction for taxpayers 65 or older, not a pension exclusion.
